name: export-workflow
description:
The three-step NQL export: a client_credentials token exchange against the login host with grant_type and scope in the x-www-form-urlencoded BODY (Okta rejects token requests whose grant_type rides the query string), a POST to /api/v1/nql/export with a JSON {"queryId": ...} body -- the documented contract; the old GET-with-query-param start was rejected by the real API -- and a status poll that reports RUNNING before COMPLETED. All three steps are routed and the poll must advance past RUNNING rather than accepting the first answer. The default query id '#runzero_integration' travels inside the JSON body, so no fragment-encoding is needed.

This scenario ends with a COMPLETED export that publishes no resultsFileUrl, which proves that case is reported cleanly with zero assets. The fourth step -- the CSV fetch itself -- is covered by download-results.json, which points resultsFileUrl back at the fixture server ($BASE is expanded inside route bodies as well as kwargs), and by download-unreachable.json for a URL that cannot be fetched at all.
